how_exchange_rates_work.heading: How exchange rates work
paragraphs: An exchange rate shows how much one currency is worth in terms of another. These values change as markets respond to inflation, interest rates, trade flows, growth expectations, and geopolitical developments.
The rate shown on ConvertCCY is intended as a reference point for comparison. It can help users estimate relative currency value before dealing with bank, card, or transfer-provider pricing.

trust_block.heading: Reference, not markup
trust_block.text: ConvertCCY is built to highlight the market relationship between currencies as clearly as possible. Customer-facing exchange rates can differ because financial institutions often apply spread, margin, or service fees.

exchange_rate_explained.heading: What an exchange rate means
paragraphs: An exchange rate is the price of one currency expressed in terms of another. It tells you how many units of the second currency you would receive in exchange for one unit of the first.

Exchange rates are not fixed. They move constantly as financial markets reassess value in response to data such as inflation reports, interest rate decisions, trade balances, and shifts in investor sentiment.

mid_market_explained.heading: What the mid-market or reference rate means
paragraphs: A reference exchange rate — sometimes called the mid-market rate — sits at the midpoint between the buy and sell prices quoted in interbank markets. It represents the purest available measure of relative currency value.

This makes it a reliable benchmark for planning, research, and comparison. When a bank or transfer service quotes you a customer rate, comparing it against the reference rate reveals how much of a spread is being applied.

bank_rate_explained.heading: Why bank and provider rates can differ
paragraphs: Retail exchange pricing typically includes a margin above the underlying market rate. That difference — sometimes called a spread or conversion fee — represents revenue for the institution providing the exchange service.

This is why the rate displayed by a bank, money-transfer platform, or travel exchange counter often differs from the reference rate shown on ConvertCCY. Knowing the reference rate helps you assess how competitive any quoted rate actually is.

market_drivers_explained.heading: What moves currencies
paragraphs: Currency values are influenced by interest rate differentials between central banks, inflation data, trade balances, capital flows, and the relative strength of each economy's growth outlook.

Some currencies are also affected by commodity prices, geopolitical risk, or safe-haven demand. During periods of global uncertainty, investors often shift capital into currencies perceived as more stable — which can move exchange rates significantly.

faq_defaults.a: The current reference exchange rate for 1 {FROM_NAME} in {TO_NAME} is shown at the top of this page. Use the converter above to check any amount in real time.

faq_defaults.q: Why does the {FROM_CODE} to {TO_CODE} rate change?
faq_defaults.a: Exchange rates change continuously as financial markets respond to new data — including central bank decisions, inflation reports, trade figures, and shifts in investor confidence. The {FROM_CODE}/{TO_CODE} rate reflects the ongoing balance of supply and demand for both currencies.

faq_defaults.q: Is the rate shown here the same as a bank rate?
faq_defaults.a: Not necessarily. The rate on ConvertCCY is a reference rate — the underlying market price between the two currencies. Banks and financial providers typically add a spread or fee on top of this, so the rate they quote to customers is usually less favorable.

faq_defaults.q: What factors affect the {FROM_CODE}/{TO_CODE} exchange rate?
faq_defaults.a: The main drivers include interest rate policy from both central banks, inflation trends, trade and current account balances, capital flows between the two economies, and broader risk sentiment in global markets.

Enter any amount in the {FROM_NAME} field above and the equivalent {TO_NAME} value will update automatically based on the current reference rate. You can also use the quick-select buttons for common amounts.

faq_defaults.q: What is the best time to exchange {FROM_CODE} to {TO_CODE}?
faq_defaults.a: There is no universally optimal time, as exchange rates fluctuate based on market conditions. However, rates tend to be most active during overlapping trading hours between major financial centres. Monitoring the reference rate over time can help you identify favorable windows.

faq_defaults.q: Can I use this rate for a money transfer?
faq_defaults.a: The rate shown here is a reference rate for informational purposes. For actual transfers, your bank or money-transfer provider will apply their own rate, which may include a spread or service fee. Always compare provider rates before sending money internationally.

remittance.q: Why is {FROM_CODE} to {TO_CODE} a common remittance corridor?
remittance.a: Some currency pairs are searched frequently because of established migration patterns, labour flows, or trade links between the two regions. Families and workers sending money across these corridors benefit from monitoring the reference rate to evaluate how much of a spread their provider is applying.

major_major.q: Why is the {FROM_CODE}/{TO_CODE} pair considered significant?
major_major.a: Currency pairs made up of major global currencies are among the most actively traded in forex markets. They serve as benchmark rates in international commerce, hedging, and financial analysis — and tend to have tighter spreads and more stable liquidity than emerging-market pairs.

major_major.q: How does central bank policy affect this major pair?
major_major.a: Both currencies in this pair are issued by central banks with significant global influence. Interest rate decisions, forward guidance, and quantitative policy shifts from either institution can move the {FROM_CODE}/{TO_CODE} rate sharply — and are closely watched by traders and analysts.

commodity_sensitive.q: Can commodity prices affect the {FROM_CODE}/{TO_CODE} rate?
commodity_sensitive.a: Yes. One or both currencies in this pair may be linked to a commodity-exporting economy. When global commodity prices rise or fall, the export revenue and economic outlook of that economy can shift — which feeds through to the exchange rate.

safe_haven_linked.q: Does global risk sentiment affect this pair?
safe_haven_linked.a: Yes. When one side of the pair has safe-haven characteristics — such as being backed by a large, stable economy with deep financial markets — periods of global uncertainty can drive demand for that currency and move the exchange rate significantly.

about.title: About ConvertCCY
about.intro: ConvertCCY is an independent digital platform designed to make currency value easier to understand across borders, markets, and everyday financial decisions.
paragraphs: Currency conversion is often presented only as a number, but the meaning behind that number matters. ConvertCCY is built to provide both a practical reference tool and a growing layer of explanation around exchange rates, relative value, and the forces that shape currency pricing.

The platform focuses on reference-first comparison. It is intended to help users understand how currencies relate to one another, while also recognising that banks and payment providers may quote different customer rates.
Over time, ConvertCCY is intended to grow into a broader reference resource for currency knowledge, market context, and practical exchange-rate understanding.

methodology.title: Methodology
paragraphs: ConvertCCY uses reference-rate logic to present the relative market value between currency pairs for informational comparison.
Exchange-rate displays on the platform should be treated as reference indicators rather than a guarantee of retail execution pricing.
Rates shown by banks, card issuers, travel desks, or transfer services can differ due to spread, markup, timing, or service fees.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
paragraphs: ConvertCCY provides informational reference content only and does not provide financial, investment, tax, legal, or transfer advice.
Users should verify actual pricing directly with financial institutions or service providers before making a transaction or relying on a quoted customer rate.
